references.text: The creation of mankind in God's image and likeness (בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ), which Genesis 5:1 refers back to with the phrase בִּדְמוּת אֱלֹהִים.
Describes the concrete creation of Adam, who is the person whose genealogy (סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת אָדָם) is introduced in Genesis 5:1.
Adam has a son in his own likeness and image, mirroring the wording in 5:1 that God created mankind in His likeness.
Reiterates that mankind was created in God's image (בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים), linking back to the creation account in Genesis 5:1.
Paul refers to Adam as the first man and contrasts him with Christ. Adam, as the ancestor of the human race, is central to the genealogy in Genesis 5:1.
Luke's genealogy traces the line all the way back to Adam, the son of God, which is directly related to the genealogy beginning in Genesis 5:1.
James states that humans are created in God's likeness (καθ᾽ ὁμοίωσιν θεοῦ), reflecting בִּדְמוּת אֱלֹהִים in Genesis 5:1.
Genesis 5:1 confirms and directly refers to the creation order found in Genesis 1:27.
